evidence.curator_note: Right-hand column of Equation 8.82, arrow labelled 'r H' pointing down from the top-right panel. Reactant: the even-electron oxocarbenium HC(=O(+)H)-(CH2)n-C(=O)-OCH3; product: the neutral aldehyde OHC-(CH2)n- with the ester now protonated on its methoxy oxygen, drawn 'H-O(+)(CH3)'. This is a PROTON transfer inside one ion, not an H-atom transfer: the ion is even-electron throughout. Book draws 2 arc(s), both FULL (double-barbed, two-electron) arrows: (i) one from the O(9)-H bond curling back onto O(9) (the bonding pair becoming a lone pair, releasing the proton) and (ii) one from the explicitly drawn lone pair (the ':' printed above the methoxy oxygen) reaching left toward that proton. Both drawn arrows begin or end on the migrating proton, which cannot carry an atom map (RDKit folds a mapped explicit H into implicit valence), so they are encoded as the one net heavy-atom-level move they produce: move <1> = the two-electron formal transfer from O(11) to O(9) (equivalently, the proton moves the other way). No implicit move is needed; the arrow gate sees no heavy-atom bond-order change, only the charge relocation, and reports the expected soft lone-pair parity notes on both oxygens. INSTANTIATION (the scheme is generic in R and in the chain length n): R = CH3 and n = 5, i.e. methyl 7-hydroxyoctanoate CH3-CH(OH)-(CH2)5-C(=O)-OCH3 (C9H18O3, M+. m/z 174.1250). n = 5 is the smallest chain that makes the final 'rH, a' step of this same scheme proceed through the favoured six-membered transition state, and it keeps the book's (CH2)n-3 label meaningful ((CH2)2). NO m/z and NO percentage is printed anywhere in Equation 8.82 except 'm/z 55' on the last product; every other mass in these records is the curator's computed monoisotopic value for this instantiation, not a measured number.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.82 (the index stops at 8.14 for Chapter 8), so no MOD rule is cross-linked to this record. No indexed rule performs an intramolecular proton transfer between two oxygens of an even-electron ion: IMS_8_11 / IMS_8_13 ('Field Rule ... rH') move an H onto an oxocarbenium but SPLIT the ion into two fragments in the same rule, and the hTransition_* families all start from an odd-electron onium site and leave a carbon radical. Unmodelled.
